page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Gram molar volume is the volume occupied by
one mole (one gram-molecular weight) of any
It is the same for every gas, because equal
numbers of gas molecules fill equal volumes.
steps.why: Avogadro's law makes the molar volume a property of the gaseous state itself, not of the particular gas — one mole of hydrogen and one mole of CO₂ fill the same volume at the same temperature and pressure.
common_mistakes: Leaving out at STP. Away from STP one mole occupies a different volume.
Restricting it to one named gas. The definition says ANY gas.
steps.memory_tip: One mole of any gas, one standard volume — the gas's identity does not matter.
steps.margin_note: The words one mole, any gas, at STP are the three marked pieces.

steps.label: The value at STP
lines: (At the newer 1 bar standard the value is 22.7 L.)
steps.why: PV = nRT with n = 1, T = 273 K and P = 1 atm gives V = 0.0821 × 273 = 22.4 L. Stating which STP is used makes the number exact rather than memorised.
common_mistakes: Writing 22.4 mL instead of 22.4 L — a thousand-fold slip.
Quoting 22.7 L against 1 atm. 22.7 L belongs to the 1 bar convention.
steps.memory_tip: One mole of ANY gas: 22.4 L at 0 °C and 1 atm.
steps.margin_note: 22.4 L is the expected board answer; the 22.7 L bracket shows the newer convention is known.

insider_note: 22.4 L is the number the examiner scans for, but writing the STP conditions beside it is what marks the answer as understood rather than recited.
